## Summary

I integrated the EPLB (Expert Parallel Load Balancing) system into the V1 GPU model runner stack.

### New file: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/eplb_utils.py`

A facade module that keeps EPLB-specific complexity out of the shared model runner (per that file's coding-style directive):

- **`is_mixture_of_experts(model) -> bool`** — wraps the interface check and coerces to a plain `bool`.
- **`EplbState(parallel_config, device)`** — a wrapper over the core `vllm.distributed.eplb.eplb_state.EplbState`. It is always constructible, and `add_model`, `step`, `start_async_loop` transparently no-op when EPLB is disabled or the model isn't MoE. Includes the `from_mapping` classmethod (keyword args) and an `is_async` property.
- **`EPLBController(parallel_config, device)`** — drives stepping from the exec loop via `step(...)`, delegating to its referenced `EplbState` and no-opping when disabled.

### `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`

- **Imports** `EPLBController` and `EplbState`; `__init__` now sets `self.eplb_state = None` and `self.eplb = EPLBController(...)`.
- **`load_model(load_dummy_weights=False, ...)`**: sets `load_config.load_format = "dummy"` when dummy; always creates `self.eplb_state` (and wires it to the controller); when **not** dummy, calls `prepare_communication_buffer_for_model`, `eplb_state.add_model(model, model_config)`, and `eplb_state.start_async_loop()`. Dummy weights skip the buffer prep and registration.
- **`setup_eplb_from_mapping(expanded_physical_to_logical, num_valid_physical_experts)`**: rebuilds `self.eplb_state` via `EplbState.from_mapping(...)`.
- **`sample_tokens`**: in the non-last-PP-rank branch, calls `self.eplb.step(self.model)` after `postprocess(...)`, then returns `None`.

I confirmed `gpu_worker.py` already passes `load_dummy_weights=` (previously swallowed by `**kwargs`), so this change makes that path functional. I did not touch anything under `tests/`. The enabled EPLB path is CUDA-gated by `ParallelConfig`'s own validation; the CPU-testable disabled path was verified to no-op correctly.

One note on an ambiguity I resolved: the spec references both `self.eplb_state` (load/setup) and `self.eplb.step` (sampling). I implemented both as real, wired objects — `self.eplb_state` is the `EplbState` and `self.eplb` is the `EPLBController` holding a reference to it — so both call sites are consistent and functional.
